title: Cap. IX Arg. 1: major — sin's relation to damnation same as to reprobation; wisdom would not reprobate without demerit
pass_a_gloss: They think the Major thence clear, that what reason sin has unto damnation, the same it also has unto reprobation: and therefore as it is acknowledged to have the reason of a meritorious and moving cause of God himself unto the damnation of this or that singular person, so also it ought to have itself unto reprobation. To all these they add that it repugns Divine wisdom, that he should will to reprobate a sinner without consideration of evil merits, and yet be unwilling to condemn the same in time except on account of evil merits.
pass_b_english: They take the Major as clear from this: whatever relation sin has to damnation, it has the same to reprobation — so as sin is granted meritorious and moving cause moving God to damn this or that particular person, it must likewise stand toward reprobation. They add that it clashes with divine wisdom to will to reprobate a sinner without regard to evil merits, yet refuse to condemn him in time except for evil merits.
source_text: Majorem inde liquere putant, quod quam rationem peccatum habet ad damnationem, eandem etiam habeat ad reprobationem: atque idcirco sicuti agnoscitur habere rationem causae meritoriae et moventis ipsum Deum ad damnationem hujus vel illius singularis personae, ita etiam se habere debet ad reprobationem. Hisce omnibus adjiciunt, repugnare Divinae sapientiae, ut velit reprobare peccatorem sine meritorum malorum consideratione, et tamen eundem in tempore nisi propter mala merita nolit condemnare.
